mainTopic: Identifying and checking the five colors of impure blood: red, black, crocus, water of earth, and diluted wine
overview: The גמרא finishes defending its definition of the red color (אדום) of impure blood. אמימר then shows his colleagues what that red looks like, and רב אשי admits that someone who cannot tell such shades apart should not rule on blood. Next, the משנה's 'black like חרת' is explained as the darkest part of dry ink, and several אמוראים give familiar samples of the black shade, such as wax, grapes, a סיואה garment, and the bath attendants' cloths. שמואל and רב יצחק בר אבודימי argue about whether black blood is checked on a white cloth or a red one. עולא, רבי אמי בר אבא, רמי בר אבא, and בר קפרא then give different views on whether shades darker or lighter than the משנה's measures are טמא or טהור. For the crocus color, the standard is moist saffron, the middle leaf of the middle layer, still in its clumps of earth, and this settles four seemingly conflicting ברייתות. Finally, the גמרא explains how to prepare the 'water of earth' sample. It ends a question about stirring by hand with תיקו and reports practical rulings on where and how the earth check may be done.

steps.title: Do reddish stains prove that a lighter red is also impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a source: רבי מאיר attributed a stain to eye salve, and רבי attributed one to sycamore sap. It then asks whether this shows they were dealing with the red color.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי מאיר attributed a stain] to eye salve, and רבי attributed a stain to sycamore sap. Isn't this talking about the red color?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes a source and uses it to challenge the earlier אמוראים who tried to define the exact shade of אדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eye salve and sycamore sap are reddish, but not exactly blood-red. If stains of that shade still had to be 'blamed' on something to avoid impurity, it seems a lighter red could also be impure blood. That would make the precise color definitions given earlier pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: An eye salve, a reddish ointment for the eyes
He attributed: he blamed the stain on something other than blood
Is it not so that...? A phrase that opens a suggested reading used as a challenge

phrases.english: to an eye salve,
and רבי attributed a stain to the sap of a sycamore.
What, is it not about the red color?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a source that began before this section and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier אמוראים who defined the exact shade of the impure red color.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If reddish stains like eye salve or sap needed to be attributed elsewhere, a lighter red must also be potentially impure, which undoes the precise definitions.

steps.title: Those stains looked like the other blood colors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the stains were not tied to אדום but to the other impure blood colors.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is about the other kinds of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge by saying those stains resembled the other blood colors in the משנה, not the red one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists several impure colors besides אדום. Eye salve or sap can look like one of those other colors. So the source tells us nothing about how light the red color may be, and the exact definitions of אדום stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The other types of blood: the other impure colors listed in the משנה

phrases.english: No, it is about the other bloods.
phrases.notes: He means the other impure colors listed in the משנה, not the red one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the source to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stains were reddish, so they were about the red color.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stains matched the other impure colors, so the definition of אדום is unaffected.
steps.whatToRemember: Attributing a stain to eye salve or sap does not prove that a lighter red is impure; those stains matched other blood colors.

steps.title: אמימר shows what the red of the משנה looks like
steps.stepSummary: While being treated by a bloodletter, אמימר points to his first blood and says this is the משנה's אדום, then says the second blood has changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר, מר זוטרא, and רב אשי were sitting before a bloodletter. He drew blood from אמימר with the first horn. אמימר looked and said: the red of the משנה is like this. He drew blood with another horn, and אמימר said: it has changed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story showing what the true אדום of the משנה looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first blood drawn is fresh and shows the exact shade of impure red. The second horn's blood already looked different, and אמימר could see the difference. This shows that the shades are subtle and need a trained eye.

keyTerms.meaning: A bloodletter, someone who draws blood for medical treatment
A horn, used by the bloodletter to draw and collect blood

phrases.english: Ameimar and Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi
were sitting before a bloodletter,
he took the first horn of blood from Ameimar,
he looked at it and said to them:
phrases.notes: It is אמימר who looks at his own blood and speaks.

phrases.english: the 'red' that we learned in the משנה is like this,
he took another horn of blood from him,
he said to them: it has changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר וּמַר זוּטְרָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי הֲווֹ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ אוּמָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the precise definition of אדום, the גמרא shows the color in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The impure אדום of the משנה looks like freshly drawn blood from the first draw.

steps.title: רב אשי: someone who can't tell the shades apart shouldn't rule on blood
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי admits he could not see the difference between the two bloods, and says a person like him should not examine blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: someone like me, who cannot tell the difference between this one and that one, should not look at blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי draws the lesson from the story: only someone with a trained eye should judge blood colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר saw a change between the two horns, but רב אשי could not. Since the הלכה depends on such fine differences, a rabbi who cannot see them should not rule on whether blood is pure or impure.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know (how to tell apart)
To look at blood: to examine it and rule on it

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
someone such as me, who does not know
the difference between this and that —
should not examine blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כְּגוֹן אֲנָא דְּלָא יָדַעְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical lesson from אמימר's demonstration.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Judging blood colors needs real expertise; one who cannot distinguish shades should not rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a standard for who may rule on blood questions: knowledge of the rules is not enough without a trained eye.
steps.whatToRemember: The shades of impure blood are subtle; only an expert who can tell them apart should rule.

steps.title: The black 'like חרת' means ink
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'black like חרת' and רבה בר רב הונא explains that חרת is ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says black is like חרת. רבה בר רב הונא said: the חרת they mentioned is ink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next color in the משנה, black, and explains the unclear word חרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה compares impure black blood to חרת, a word the reader may not know. רבה בר רב הונא identifies it as ink, giving a clear standard for this shade.

keyTerms.meaning: Black: one of the impure blood colors
The word the משנה uses for the black standard

phrases.english: Black — like חרת.
Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
the חרת they spoke of — is ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the next color in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The black of the משנה is the color of ink.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports that the black is ink
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says black is like חרת and that the black they meant is ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: black is like חרת, and the black they spoke of is ink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא backs up the explanation from an earlier, תנאי source. It also uses both words, חרת and ink, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Also like this: a source that agrees with what was just said

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a ברייתא:
black is like חרת,
and the black they spoke of — is ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה בר רב הונא's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: That the חרת of the משנה is ink.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the black they spoke of is ink.

steps.title: Why not just say 'ink'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא mentions חרת at all, instead of simply saying ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it just say 'ink'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording: if the black is ink, why use two terms?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ink is the standard, saying 'like חרת' seems like extra wording. The גמרא assumes every word in a source teaches something, so it asks what חרת adds.

keyTerms.meaning: So let it say...: a challenge suggesting simpler wording

phrases.english: So let it say 'ink'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the double wording of the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the black is simply ink, the word חרת seems unnecessary.

steps.title: חרת means the darkest part of the ink
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'ink' alone could mean the clear top layer, so חרת teaches it means the dark bottom part.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had said only 'ink', I would think it means the clear part of the ink. It teaches us it means the dark part of the ink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the word חרת tells us which part of the ink is the standard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ink in an inkwell has a lighter, clearer top layer and a darker bottom. Saying only 'ink' could point to the lighter part. חרת (related to חרותא, blackness) shows the standard is the darkest part.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought: the mistaken assumption without the extra word
The clear, lighter part of the ink
The blackness: the dark part of the ink
It teaches us: what the extra wording comes to tell

phrases.english: If it had said 'ink' —
I would have said it is like the clear part of the ink,

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כִּי חֲרוּתָא דִּדְיוֹתָא.
phrases.english: it teaches us it is like the blackness of the ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining that the extra word prevents a mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'ink', one might think the lighter, clear part of the ink is the standard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The standard is the dark part of the ink, which the word חרת signals.
steps.whatToRemember: Impure black blood is compared to ink, and specifically to its darkest part, not the lighter top layer.

steps.title: Is the measuring ink wet or dry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the חרת ink used to measure black blood is moist ink or dry ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: is it moist ink or dry ink?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now knows the measure is the dark part of ink. It asks a follow-up question: should that ink be wet or dried?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wet ink and dry ink can look like different shades of black. Since the color of the blood decides between pure and impure, the exact measuring sample has to be pinned down.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised (an open question the גמרא wants to settle)

phrases.english: A question was asked to them:
With moist or with dry?
phrases.notes: He means the ink (חרת) from the last step: should we compare the blood to wet ink or dried ink?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down the ink definition from Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ink used as the measure is wet or dry.

steps.title: רבי אמי used dry ink
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from practice: רבי אמי broke off a lump of dried ink and checked blood against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אמי would break off a lump of ink and check the blood with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to what רבי אמי actually did. You can only break off a lump from dry ink, so the measure is dry ink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one states a rule here. The answer comes from a real-life practice: a 'lump' of ink can only be dry ink. That settles the question as dry.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For Rabbi Ami would break off a lump of ink
and examine the blood with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי פָּלֵי קוּרְטָא דִּדְיוֹתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dry ink, as seen from רבי אמי's practice of breaking off lumps of it.
steps.whatToRemember: The ink used to measure black blood is the dark part of dry ink.

steps.title: שמואל: wax, ink, and grape colors are impure
steps.stepSummary: שמואל lists black shades that make a woman impure and ties them to the משנה's words 'deeper than that is impure'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: blood like black wax, ink, or a black grape is impure. This is what we learned: 'deeper than that is impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section explaining the משנה's line about blood darker or lighter than ink. שמואל gives examples of black shades that are impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of measuring only against ink, שמואל gives familiar objects as samples of the impure shade. He says these are what the משנה means by 'deeper than that'.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Like wax, like ink, and like a grape, she is impure,
and this is what we learned:
'Deeper than that, impure.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּקִיר, כִּדְיוֹ וּכְעֵנָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the ink to the משנה's rule about shades darker than ink.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood the color of black wax, ink, or a black grape is impure. This is the 'deeper than that' of the משנה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: olive, tar, and raven colors are pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר lists lighter black shades that are pure and ties them to the משנה's words 'lighter than that is pure'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: blood like a black olive, tar, or a raven is pure. This is what we learned: 'lighter than that is pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the other side: examples of blacks that are lighter than the measure, so the blood is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave samples for the impure side. רבי אלעזר gives samples for the pure side, matching the משנה's 'lighter than that'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Like an olive, like tar, and like a raven, it is pure,
and this is what we learned:
'Lighter than that, pure.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כְּזַיִת, כְּזֶפֶת וּכְעוֹרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the pure side to match שמואל's impure side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood the color of a black olive, tar, or a raven is pure. This is the 'lighter than that' of the משנה.

steps.title: עולא: like a סיואה garment
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the black of the משנה is like the color of a garment from סיואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: like a סיואה garment.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives his own picture of the impure black color, this time a type of clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא picks a well-known dark garment as the sample shade. The next step shows how he pointed out this color in real life.

keyTerms.meaning: From סיואה, a place known for very black garments

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Like a Siva'a garment.
phrases.notes: A garment from a place called סיואה, whose clothes were known to be very black.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another definition of the black shade, alongside שמואל and רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The impure black is like a סיואה garment.

steps.title: עולא points out the black garment in פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: In פומבדיתא, עולא saw an Arab in a black garment and said that is the black of the משנה. People tore pieces off it as samples and paid him 400 זוזים.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא came to פומבדיתא and saw an Arab wearing a black garment. He said: 'The black we learned about is like this.' They tore it off him bit by bit and gave him four hundred zuz.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows עולא's definition in action. He found a real example of the shade, and people took pieces of the garment to keep as samples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story turns עולא's words into a usable sample. People valued having the exact shade for checking blood so much that they paid a large sum for the pieces.

phrases.english: Ulla happened to come to Pumbedita,
he saw a certain Arab
who was wearing a black garment.
He said to them:
The 'black' that we learned about is like this.
They tore it from him bit by bit,
and they gave him four hundred zuz for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing עולא's definition from Step 13 in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The black of the משנה is like the black garment עולא saw in פומבדיתא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: like the bath attendants' cloths from overseas
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the black of the משנה is like the cloths of bath attendants that come from overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: these are the cloths of the bath attendants that come from overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: One more אמורא gives a sample for the black shade: a known type of cloth used by bath attendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן also uses cloth as the sample, but a different kind from עולא's. The גמרא will now question whether these cloths are really black.

keyTerms.meaning: Overseas, a land across the sea

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
These are the cloths of the bath attendants
phrases.notes: Here כֵּלִים means cloths or garments, not utensils.

phrases.english: that come from overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵלּוּ כֵּלִים הָאוֹלְיָירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another definition of the black shade, different from עולא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The impure black is like the bath attendants' cloths from overseas.

steps.title: Are those cloths really black? רבי ינאי's burial request
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: רבי ינאי asked to be buried in these cloths because they are neither black nor white. So how can they be the black of the משנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say they are black? But רבי ינאי told his sons: Don't bury me in black or in white. Not black, in case I am found worthy and look like a mourner among grooms. Not white, in case I am not found worthy and look like a groom among mourners. Rather, bury me in the cloths of the bath attendants from overseas. So it seems they are not black!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's definition. It brings רבי ינאי, who chose these exact cloths because they are a middle color, not black.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי wanted something neither black nor white, and he picked the bath attendants' cloths. That shows those cloths are an in-between shade. If so, they cannot serve as the sample for 'black' blood, as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a challenge to what was just said)
I will merit, be found worthy (in heavenly judgment)
So it seems, which shows that (draws a conclusion)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ינאי's story is not about the הלכה of burial here. The גמרא uses it only to show what color the bath attendants' cloths were.

phrases.english: Is that to say that they are black?
But didn't Rabbi Yannai say to his sons:
My sons, do not bury me

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בְּכֵלִים שְׁחוֹרִים וְלֹא בְּכֵלִים לְבָנִים.
phrases.english: neither in black clothes nor in white clothes.
Not black, in case I am found worthy
and I will be like a mourner among grooms,
Not white, in case I am not found worthy
and I will be like a groom among mourners,
Rather, bury me in the cloths of the bath attendants
that come from overseas.
So it seems they are not black!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּאוּכָּמֵי נִינְהוּ? וְהָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יַנַּאי לְבָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's definition from Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the black of the משנה is like the bath attendants' cloths.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ינאי chose these cloths because they are neither black nor white, so they cannot be the sample for black blood.

steps.title: Same cloth, different look: worn as a garment or spread on a table
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: when worn as a garment these cloths are not black, and when spread on a table they are black.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult: this one is about a garment, and that one is about a table.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from רבי ינאי. A cloth worn as a garment is not counted as black, but the same kind of cloth spread on a table is the black of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי was talking about the cloth as a garment, where it looks neither black nor white. רבי יוחנן was talking about the cloth spread flat over a table, where it shows as black. So both statements can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. The opening words of an answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is about a garment,
phrases.notes: Meaning רבי ינאי, who was talking about the cloth worn on the body.

phrases.english: That is about a table.
phrases.notes: Meaning רבי יוחנן, who was talking about the cloth spread over a table.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא — הָא בִּגְלִימָא, הָא בְּפָתוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): two different ways the same cloth is used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ינאי's words seemed to show these cloths are never black, which would go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: As a garment the cloth is not considered black. Spread on a table it is black, and that is the black of the משנה.

steps.title: All blood colors are checked on a white cloth
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: all the blood colors are checked only on a white cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: and all of them are checked only on a white cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how to check the colors of the blood. שמואל says every color must be checked on a white cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was defining what each shade looks like. Now it gives a practical rule for how to see the shade correctly: put the blood on a white cloth.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of them (all the blood colors of the משנה)

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
And all of them, we check them only
on top of a white cloth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְכוּלָּם, אֵין בּוֹדְקִין אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי מַטְלֵית לְבָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the shade of black to the method of checking all the colors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every blood color is checked only on a white cloth.

steps.title: Black blood is checked on a red cloth
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבודימי says black blood is checked on a red cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבודימי said: and black is checked on a red cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds that black blood is checked on a red cloth. This sets up the question in the next steps: does he argue with שמואל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said all colors go on white. רב יצחק בר אבודימי says black goes on red. That seems to clash with שמואל, at least for black.

phrases.english: רב יצחק בר אבודימי said:
And black is checked on top of a red cloth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי: וְשָׁחוֹר עַל גַּבֵּי אָדוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different background color for black, which seems to differ from שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Black blood is checked on a red cloth.

steps.title: They do not argue: black on red, the rest on white
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדפתי says the two rulings do not argue. רב יצחק בר אבודימי is talking about black, and שמואל is talking about the other colors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה מדפתי said: they do not argue. This one is about black, and that one is about the other bloods.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה מדפתי tries to show that שמואל and רב יצחק בר אבודימי agree. Each one is talking about different colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this answer, שמואל's 'all of them' means all colors except black, and those go on white. Black goes on red. So there is no argument.

phrases.english: רב ירמיה from דפתי said:
And they do not argue:
This one is about black,
phrases.notes: This one means רב יצחק בר אבודימי's red cloth.

phrases.english: and that one is about the other bloods.
phrases.notes: That one means שמואל's white cloth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה מִדִּפְתִּי: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי — הָא בְּשָׁחוֹר, הָא בִּשְׁאָר דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the seeming clash between steps 18 and 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ruling covers different colors
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like שמואל and רב יצחק בר אבודימי argue about how to check black.
steps.terutzMaskana: Black is checked on red, and the other colors on white, so there is no argument.

steps.title: Then שמואל should have said 'except for black'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects: if שמואל agreed that black is different, he should have said 'except for black'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: if so, let שמואל say 'except for black'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רב ירמיה מדפתי's answer. If שמואל really meant to leave out black, he would have said so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said 'all of them', with no exception. If black needed a red cloth, he should have said 'all except black'. Since he did not, his words seem to include black too.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it (a strong challenge)

phrases.english: רב אשי objected to it:
If so, let שמואל say
"except for black"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אִי הָכִי, לֵימָא שְׁמוּאֵל ״חוּץ מִשָּׁחוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ירמיה מדפתי's claim that שמואל's rule does not include black.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל said 'all of them' with no exception. If black were left out, he would have said 'except for black'.

steps.title: They argue about black itself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes that שמואל and רב יצחק בר אבודימי really do argue about how to check black blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: they argue about black itself.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the 'no argument' answer, רב אשי says plainly that the two sages really argue about black blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, black is checked on white like all the other colors. For רב יצחק בר אבודימי, black is checked on red. The argument is only about black.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier idea and gives a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: All colors besides black: everyone agrees they are checked on a white cloth. Black: שמואל says white, and רב יצחק בר אבודימי says red.

phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said:
They argue about black itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּשָׁחוֹר גּוּפֵיהּ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 20 with a new understanding.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting that there is a real argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ירמיה מדפתי thought the two rulings cover different colors.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל includes black in the white-cloth rule, so he and רב יצחק בר אבודימי argue about black.

steps.title: For every color: darker is impure, lighter is pure, just like black
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the משנה's rule for black, that darker is טמא and lighter is טהור, applies to all five colors.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: for all of them, deeper than that is impure, and lighter than that is pure, like black.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא takes the rule the משנה said only about black and applies it to every blood color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said about black that a darker shade is טמא and a lighter shade is טהור. עולא says the same is true for each of the five colors. A shade darker than the משנה's shade is טמא, and a lighter shade is טהור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives one simple rule for judging the shades of all the colors, not only black.

phrases.english: עולא said:
For all of them, deeper than that is impure,
lighter than that is pure,
like black.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: כּוּלָּן, עָמוֹק מִכֵּן — טָמֵא, דֵּיהֶה מִכֵּן — טָהוֹר, כַּשָּׁחוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement that widens the משנה's rule for black to all the colors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For all five colors, a darker shade is טמא and a lighter shade is טהור, just as the משנה says about black.

steps.title: Why did the משנה mention only black?
steps.stepSummary: If עולא is right that the darker/lighter rule applies to all five colors, why does the משנה state it only about black?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, what is special about black, that the משנה mentions this rule only for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא from Step 23. If the rule covers every color, the משנה should not have tied it to black alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only about black that darker is טמא and lighter is טהור. Normally, when the משנה names one case, we assume the rule belongs to that case alone. So עולא's broad reading needs to explain why black is singled out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why is this case singled out?
It mentioned, it chose to state
Black, one of the five colors of טמא blood

phrases.english: But if so, what is different
about black, that the משנה mentions it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's statement in Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that the rule for black applies to all five colors
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה states the rule only for black. That suggests it belongs only to black.

steps.title: Black needed its own mention because of רבי חנינא's idea
steps.stepSummary: Black is really red that has been spoiled, so we might have thought even lighter black is טמא. The משנה teaches that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since רבי חנינא says black is really red that has been damaged, even black that is lighter than the משנה's shade should be טמא. So the משנה teaches us that lighter black is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא. The משנה spelled out the rule for black because black is the one color where we might have made a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Black blood is really red blood that has been spoiled. So we might think any black shade, even a light one, is still basically red and טמא. The משנה mentions black so we do not think that. The rule itself still applies to all colors.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the mistaken idea the source comes to prevent)

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
since Rabbi Chanina says
"Black is red, only it was damaged,"
therefore even if it is lighter than that
it should also be impure?
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why one case needed to be stated (to prevent a mistaken assumption)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since black is really red, even light black would be טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: Lighter black is טהור. The rule is stated for black only to block that mistake, but it applies to all colors.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps עולא's view standing: darker is טמא and lighter is טהור for all five colors.

steps.title: רבי אמי בר אבא: darker or lighter, all are טמא except black
steps.stepSummary: For all colors except black, a shade darker or lighter than the משנה's measure is still טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי בר אבא says: For all the colors, darker than the measure is impure, and lighter is also impure, except for black.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion argues with עולא. רבי אמי בר אבא is stricter for all the colors other than black.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עולא, lighter is טהור for every color. For רבי אמי בר אבא, lighter is טהור only for black, as the משנה says. All the other colors stay טמא even when lighter.

keyTerms.meaning: Deeper or darker than that shade

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami bar Abba says:
And all of them: deeper than that, impure;
lighter than that, also impure,
except for black.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר וְכוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from עולא's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every color except black is טמא whether it is darker or lighter than the משנה's measure.

steps.title: Then what are the measures for?
steps.stepSummary: If darker and lighter are both טמא, the חכמים's exact color measures seem pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what use are the measures of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי בר אבא. If any shade counts, why did the משנה describe each color so exactly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives exact descriptions for each color. If shades darker and lighter are also טמא, those descriptions do not seem to rule anything out.

keyTerms.meaning: The measures set by the חכמים (the color descriptions in the משנה)

phrases.english: But what purpose do the measures of the Sages serve?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי בר אבא's view in Step 26
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both darker and lighter are טמא, the exact descriptions in the משנה seem to have no purpose.

steps.title: The measures rule out a very faint shade
steps.stepSummary: The measures exclude a color that is far lighter, lighter than lighter.
steps.simpleTranslation: They come to exclude a shade that is lighter than lighter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the measures still matter, because a shade far lighter than the measure is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shade a little lighter is still טמא in this view. A shade that is much lighter is no longer counted as טמא blood. The measure is the starting point for telling where that line is.

keyTerms.meaning: Lighter than lighter, a very faint shade

phrases.english: To exclude a shade lighter than lighter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the measures exclude an extreme case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The measures do nothing if darker and lighter are both טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: The measures exclude a very faint shade, which is טהור

steps.title: Another version: רמי בר אבא says darker or lighter, all are טהור except black
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the statement says the opposite: any change from the measure makes the blood טהור, except for black.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רמי בר אבא says: For all the colors, darker than the measure is pure and lighter is pure, except for black. That is why the measures of the חכמים matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, opposite version of the previous statement. Here every color must match the measure exactly, or the blood is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version is the most lenient. Only the exact shade is טמא. Black is the exception: darker black is טמא, as the משנה says. In this view the measures clearly matter, since any change from them makes the blood טהור.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In רבי אמי בר אבא's version, darker or lighter is טמא. In רמי בר אבא's version, darker or lighter is טהור.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Rami bar Abba says:
And all of them: deeper than that, pure;
lighter than that, pure,
except for black,
and for this the measures of the Sages are effective.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא אֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, opposite version of Step 26's statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every color except black is טמא only at the exact shade. Darker or lighter is טהור.

steps.title: בר קפרא: darker is טמא, lighter is טהור, except diluted wine
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא agrees with the general rule (darker טמא, lighter טהור), but for the diluted-wine color both darker and lighter are טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא says: For all the colors, darker is impure and lighter is pure, except for diluted wine, where darker is pure and lighter is also pure.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion. בר קפרא keeps עולא's general pattern but makes one exception, the color of diluted wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For most colors, בר קפרא follows the simple rule: darker is טמא and lighter is טהור. For מזג, only the exact shade is טמא, and any change either way makes the blood טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Diluted wine, the color of one of the five kinds of טמא blood

phrases.english: Bar Kappara says:
And all of them: deeper than that, impure;
lighter than that, pure.
Except for diluted wine,
where deeper than that is pure,
and lighter than that is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another view on how far the measures stretch
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Darker is טמא and lighter is טהור for all colors. For מזג, any change from the exact shade is טהור.

steps.title: בר קפרא is tested and rules טהור both ways
steps.stepSummary: They made diluted-wine blood lighter and darker, and both times בר קפרא ruled it טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They lightened it before בר קפרא and he ruled it pure. They darkened it and he ruled it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that בר קפרא really ruled by his own rule about מזג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both changes, lighter and darker, led to a טהור ruling, just as he said in Step 30. He could see the small difference from the exact shade and acted on it.

phrases.english: Before Bar Kappara they lightened it, and he ruled it pure;
they deepened it, and he ruled it pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows בר קפרא acting on his ruling from Step 30
steps.raayaObject: בר קפרא's rule that מזג is טהור whether darker or lighter
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case where בר קפרא ruled טהור in both directions

steps.title: רבי חנינא praises בר קפרא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא praises בר קפרא, whose sharp eye matched his ruling of הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: How great is a man whose heart matches his teaching!
steps.whatsHappening: The section ends with רבי חנינא's praise of בר קפרא for living up to his own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling on such small color differences takes great skill. בר קפרא's judgment in practice matched exactly what he taught.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on shades darker or lighter than the משנה's measure. עולא: darker טמא, lighter טהור, for all colors. רבי אמי בר אבא: both טמא, except black. רמי בר אבא: both טהור, except black. בר קפרא: like עולא, except מזג, which is טהור both ways.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
How great is the man
whose heart is in accordance with his teaching!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording in square brackets means "like his teaching."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא כַּמָּה נְפִישׁ גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Praises בר קפרא after the story in Step 31
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בר קפרא's practical judgment matched his ruling on מזג, and רבי חנינא admired him for it.

steps.title: Saffron color means fresh, moist saffron
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's color כקרן כרכום, and a ברייתא clarifies that it means moist saffron, not dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one טמא color is 'like the bright part of the crocus.' A ברייתא taught: this means moist saffron, not dry saffron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the next blood color listed in the משנה and quotes a ברייתא that pins down what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saffron changes color as it dries. The ברייתא tells us to use the fresh, moist saffron as the measuring standard. Dry saffron looks different and is not the standard.

keyTerms.meaning: The bright part of the crocus flower, which is used to make saffron

phrases.english: And like the bright part of the crocus.
It was taught: moist, and not dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of diluted wine and בר קפרא, and moves to the next color in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The saffron standard is moist saffron, not dry.

steps.title: Four teachings disagree about which part of the flower
steps.stepSummary: Four ברייתות give opposite answers about whether the lower or the upper part of the crocus is the standard.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא says: like the lower part, not like the upper. Another says: like the upper, not like the lower. Another says: like the upper, and all the more so like the lower. Another says: like the lower, and all the more so like the upper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up four ברייתות that seem to flatly contradict each other. This sets up the problem that אביי will solve next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two ברייתות directly oppose each other: lower only, versus upper only. The last two also oppose each other about which part is the main standard and which one counts 'all the more so.' The contradiction is not stated out loud as a question, but it is clearly the problem that needs an answer.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is choosing one ברייתא over the others. The goal is to show that all four are right, each talking from a different angle.

phrases.english: One teaching says: like the lower part, not like the upper.
And another teaching says: like the upper part, and not like the lower.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: כָּעֶלְיוֹן, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן כַּתַּחְתּוֹן.
phrases.english: And another teaching says: like the upper part, and all the more so like the lower.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: כַּתַּחְתּוֹן, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן כָּעֶלְיוֹן.
phrases.english: And another teaching says: like the lower part, and all the more so like the upper.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: כַּתַּחְתּוֹן, לֹא כָּעֶלְיוֹן. וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the saffron standard from step 33 and asks which part of the flower is meant, bringing four sources that conflict.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the ברייתות about which part of the crocus is the color standard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each ברייתא picks a different part as the standard, or reverses which part counts 'all the more so,' so they cannot all be right at face value.

steps.title: אביי: the flower has three layers of three leaves
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins his answer: the crocus has three layers, and each layer has three leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: there are three layers and three leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts solving the contradiction by describing how the flower is built. This sets up his practical rule in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there are several layers and several leaves, 'upper' and 'lower' become relative words. A middle piece is 'upper' compared to the one below it and 'lower' compared to the one above it. That is the key that will make the four ברייתות fit together.

phrases.english: אביי said:
There are three layers and three leaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תְּלָתָא דָּרֵי וּתְלָתָא טַרְפֵי הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual description that makes 'upper' and 'lower' relative terms.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to be talking about one simple upper part and one simple lower part.
steps.terutzMaskana: The flower has several levels, so each ברייתא can be describing the same piece from a different side.

steps.title: Use the middle leaf of the middle layer
steps.stepSummary: The standard is the middle leaf of the middle layer, and this reconciles all four ברייתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take the middle layer, and hold the middle leaf in your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the practical rule: compare the blood to the middle leaf of the middle layer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first pair of ברייתות is about layers. The middle layer is 'lower' than the top layer and 'upper' than the bottom layer. The second pair is about leaves within the middle layer. Each one says that blood like an outer leaf, lower or upper, is impure, and blood like the middle leaf is impure all the more so.
steps.whatToRemember: For the saffron color, the standard is fresh saffron, and specifically the middle leaf of the middle layer. 'Upper' and 'lower' in the four ברייתות are relative to that middle piece, so they do not really argue.

phrases.english: Take the middle layer,
and the middle leaf, in your hand.
phrases.notes: Both words mean 'middle.' Some versions have the one in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected spelling.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְקוֹט דָּרָא מְצִיעָאָה, וְטַרְפָּא מְצִיעָא בִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer from step 35 with the practical rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Compare the blood to the middle leaf of the middle layer of fresh saffron. Read this way, all four ברייתות agree.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the crocus must still be in its clumps of earth
steps.stepSummary: When people brought blood to רבי אבהו to compare with the crocus color, he ruled that the standard is a crocus still in its clumps of earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: When people came to רבי אבהו to have blood checked, he told them: we learned that the crocus is compared while it is still in its clumps of earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רבי אבהו handled real cases: he insisted that the comparison crocus be one still in its clumps of earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 33-36 already set the standard: moist saffron, the middle leaf of the middle layer. רבי אבהו adds one more practical condition: the flower must still be in the earth it grew in. A loose, picked flower is not the standard.

keyTerms.meaning: their clumps of earth, the soil the flowers grew in

steps.whatToRemember: The crocus standard is moist saffron, the middle leaf of the middle layer, and still in its clumps of earth.

phrases.english: When they would come before Rabbi Abbahu,
he would say to them:
We learned: in their clumps of earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final practical condition to the crocus standard explained in steps 33-36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The crocus used for comparison must be one still in its clumps of earth.

steps.title: Which valley's earth is used for the 'water of earth' color
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next color in the משנה. A ברייתא records a dispute over which valley's earth one should use.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'like the water of earth.' A ברייתא explains: one brings fertile earth from the בית כרם valley and floods it with water, according to רבי מאיר. רבי עקיבא says from the יודפת valley. רבי יוסי says from the סכני valley. רבי שמעון says even from the גנוסר valley and similar places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next color in the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains how to make the comparison sample. The תנאים argue about which valley's earth to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic: the color כמימי אדמה, earth with water poured over it. Every opinion agrees on the method, which is fertile earth with water flooded over it. They argue only about where the earth comes from. רבי שמעון is the most lenient: any valley with similar soil is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: like the water of earth: the color of water mixed with reddish soil
floods, pours water over until it covers

phrases.english: "And like the water of earth."
The Rabbis taught: "Like the water of earth" —
one brings fertile earth
from the Beit Kerem Valley,
and floods water over it,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Akiva says: from the Yodfat Valley.
Rabbi Yosei says: from the Sikhnei Valley.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף מִבִּקְעַת גִּנּוֹסַר
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: even from the Genosar Valley
and places like them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the crocus color to the next color in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The water-of-earth sample is made by flooding fertile earth with water. The תנאים argue over which valley's earth qualifies.

steps.title: How to prepare the muddy water sample
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא gives the exact method: water a garlic-peel's thickness above the earth, no fixed amount, check it only while muddy, and re-stir with a vessel, not by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: one brings fertile earth from the בית כרם valley and floods it with water about as thick as a garlic peel. There is no set amount of water, because there is no set amount of earth. One does not check the blood against clear water, only against muddy water. If the water became clear, one stirs it up again. When stirring it, one does not do so by hand, only with a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with practical instructions for making and using the muddy water sample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא follows רבי מאיר's valley but adds new details. The water level is only relative, a thin layer over the earth. The total amounts do not matter, as long as a thin layer of water, about a garlic peel's thickness, covers the earth. The color is only valid while the water is cloudy, and the stirring must be done with a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: like the thickness of a garlic peel: a very thin layer
clear (the earth has settled to the bottom)
stirs them up, makes them muddy

steps.confusionAlert: "No measure for the water" does not mean any amount of water works. The layer must still be about a garlic peel's thickness above the earth. It only means the total quantity does not matter, since any amount of earth is fine.

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא: "And like the water of earth" —

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא אֲדָמָה שְׁמֵנָה מִבִּקְעַת בֵּית כֶּרֶם,
phrases.english: one brings fertile earth from the Beit Kerem Valley,
and floods water over it like the thickness of a garlic peel,
and there is no fixed amount for the water,
because there is no fixed amount for the earth,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתָן צְלוּלִין, אֶלָּא עֲכוּרִין.
phrases.english: and one does not check against them when clear, only when muddy.
If they became clear, one stirs them up again,
and when he stirs them up,
he does not stir them by hand, only with a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא on the same color, adding practical details about preparing the sample.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water a garlic-peel's thickness above the earth. Amounts do not matter. Compare only while muddy, and re-stir with a vessel, not by hand.

steps.title: What does 'not by hand but with a vessel' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא's last rule means. Is it only forbidding holding the earth in your hand, or does it also forbid stirring by hand when the earth is in a vessel?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: when it says one does not stir them by hand, only with a vessel, does that mean one should not put the earth in his hand and stir with it, but if the earth is in a vessel, stirring with his hand is fine? Or perhaps it means one must not stir it by hand at all, only with a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the exact meaning of the ברייתא's last line. This sets up steps 41-43, which try to settle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible readings. In the first, the problem is holding the earth in your hand while mixing; if the earth sits in a vessel, using your hand to stir is fine. In the second, any stirring done with the hand is forbidden, and the stirring itself must be done with a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised before them: an open question the גמרא tries to settle
or perhaps: introduces the second side of a question

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹכְרִין אוֹתָן בַּיָּד אֶלָּא בִּכְלִי —
phrases.english: "One does not stir them by hand, only with a vessel" —
does it mean he should not put it in his hand and stir them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּמָנָא כִּי עָכַר לֵיהּ בִּידֵיהּ —
phrases.english: but when it is in a vessel and he stirs it with his hand,
it is fine?
Or perhaps he should not stir them with his hand at all,
only with a vessel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read the final instruction of the ברייתא in step 39.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ban on stirring 'by hand' only forbids holding the earth in your hand, or also forbids hand-stirring when the earth is in a vessel.

steps.title: A proof: the check is done only in a cup
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying the earth-water is checked only in a cup, which seems to show a vessel is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When one checks it, he checks it only in a cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 40 with a ברייתא saying the checking must be done in a cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 40 asked whether only holding the earth in your hand is forbidden, or also stirring by hand even when the earth is in a vessel. This ברייתא says a cup must be used. That seems to show a vessel is required for the whole process.

keyTerms.meaning: He checks them (comparing the blood to the earth-water)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
When he checks them,
he checks them only in a cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to resolve the שאלה of step 40.
steps.raayaObject: That a vessel, not the hand, must be used in the process.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the checking is done only in a cup.

steps.title: The proof fails: checking is not the same as stirring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא speaks about the checking being in a cup, but says nothing about what the stirring is done with.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you can still ask your question: The checking is in a cup, but what is the muddying done with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 41 and says it does not answer our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate actions: checking the color and stirring the mud (עכירה). The ברייתא only says the checking must be in a cup. Whether you may stir with your hand once the earth is in the cup is still unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: You can still ask your question; the doubt stays
Making the water muddy again by stirring

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two actions. A cup is required for the checking, but that alone does not tell us whether the hand may do the stirring.

phrases.english: But you can still ask your question:
the checking is in a cup,
but what is the muddying done with?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 39, where the mud is stirred up again before each check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 41.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא speaks only about the checking, not the stirring, which is what the question was about.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the question about stirring by hand with תיקו: it stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question from step 40 without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settled whether stirring by hand inside a vessel is allowed. So the question is left open as a תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved
A question or dilemma the גמרא asks

steps.whatToRemember: A cup must be used for checking. Whether the stirring may be done by hand in a vessel is a תיקו, an unresolved question.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question after the proof was rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of stirring by hand in a vessel remains unresolved.

steps.title: The earth check works only in its own place
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה told people who came to him that the earth check works only in the place the earth comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: When people came before רבה בר אבוה, he said to them: We learned that the check is done in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a practical ruling: רבה בר אבוה would not do the earth-water check away from where the earth came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 38 told us which valley's earth to use. רבה בר אבוה adds a limit: the check only works in that place. If the earth is carried somewhere else, it cannot be used.

keyTerms.meaning: In its place, where the earth comes from

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: When they came before Rabba bar Avuh,
he said to them:
We learned it is "in its place."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תיקו, moves to a practical report about how the earth check is used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth-water check is valid only in the earth's own place.

steps.title: Checking with a dry clump of earth is condemned
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא checked blood by breaking up a clump of earth without water, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי cursed this practice with אסכרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא would break up a clump of earth and check with it. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי cursed over it with אסכרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבי חנינא checked with crumbled dry earth, and that רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי strongly condemned it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 39 said the earth must be mixed with water and checked while muddy. Checking against a dry clump skips that method. The harsh curse shows how seriously this shortcut was rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: The earth check must follow the method of step 39: earth mixed with water and checked while muddy, in its own place. Shortcuts like a dry clump were sharply rejected.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina would break up a clump of earth
and check with it,
phrases.notes: He did this without mixing it in water, unlike the method in step 39.

phrases.aramaic: לָיֵיט עֲלֵיהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei cursed over it
with diphtheria.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical report about how the earth check must be done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Checking with a dry clump of earth is not acceptable and was harshly condemned.
